For us the inner union is enough: one that is not contrary to nature and does not destroy the truth of Christ's body, which rests on a principle both physical and theological, but is supernatural, purely divine and heavenly; and that faith which searches the deep things of God revealed to us in the Word and sealed in the Sacraments, which holds the mind of God concerning the mystery of our salvation, and which, relying on the power of Almighty God, carries us up even into heaven. Rightly, therefore, Chrysostom says to the people of Antioch in homily 61 that Christ presents himself to us in these mysteries, to be not only seen but also touched and handled. Yet not certainly with the eyes of the body, the hand, or the mouth, but by spiritual contact through faith; and that not on earth but in heaven, lest he refute himself, whose words we cited above.

units.la: Sed age,hoc quoque eorundem argumen-tum audiamus. Nihil ultra naturam & modum essentiae sua agit vel operatur, & oppositorum ea-dem est ratio. Sicut ergo Spiritum seu spiritualem essentiam corporaliter, (id est, corporali essen-tiae modo) adesse pro impossibili recte habetur: i-ta si corpus Christi verum & non imaginarium ve-re adest in Coena, sicut cordatiores Caluinistae vi-deri volunt afferere, necesse est omnino, non ut spi-ritualiter, sed corporaliter adsint. At enim si haec vera semel, quinam omne tum Transubstan-tationis, tum Consubstantiationis & Ubi-quitatis fundamentum non ruet? Nam si non aliter adest in Coena verum illud Christi corpus quàm modo illo corporeis omnibus rebus proprio & merè naturali: Ergo circum-scriptiuè & localiter & visibiliter adest, quia naturale & organicum omne corpus illud est quod verè videri & tangi potest. Ubi igitur, & qua tandem in huius actionis parte ma-gnum illud coniugij inter Christum & Ec-clesiam suam initi mysterium invenietur, quod tam altè & tam expresse testificatur Apostolus? Corporalis enim ille & corpo-ribus omnibus communis modus quid mysticum & arcanum habet, siue ad signorum & rerum, siue ad rerum significatarum perceptionem modus ille, accommodetur? Et quodnam erit inter naturale inter homines,& spirituale, ac merè cœleste ac divinum inter Christum & Ecclesiam suam contra-ctum coniugium discrimen? Et cur nos,nō v-nam carnem naturali copula, sed unum, non numero,sed spirituali modo & efficacia,Spi-ritum cum Christo fieri qui per fidem illi ad-hæremus,diserte scripserit Apostolus?
units.tr: But come, let us hear this argument of theirs too. "Nothing acts or operates beyond the nature and mode of its essence, and the same reasoning holds for opposites. Therefore, just as it is rightly considered impossible for the Spirit, or a spiritual essence, to be present corporeally (that is, in the mode of a bodily essence), so, if the true body of Christ is really present in the Supper, as the more discerning Calvinists want to maintain, it must necessarily be present not spiritually but corporeally." But once this is granted, who does not see that the foundation of all transubstantiation, consubstantiation and ubiquity collapses? For if the true body of Christ is present in the Supper in no other way than that mode which belongs to all corporeal things and is purely natural, then it is present circumscriptively, locally and visibly, since every natural and organic body is one that can truly be seen and touched. Where, then, and in what part of this action will that great mystery of the marriage between Christ and his Church be found, which the Apostle attests so deeply and so expressly? For does that bodily mode, common to all bodies, have anything mystical and secret about it, whether it is adapted to the perception of the signs and things or of the things signified? And what difference will there be between the natural marriage among men and the spiritual, purely heavenly and divine marriage contracted between Christ and his Church? And why did the Apostle plainly write that we who cleave to the Lord by faith become one spirit with Christ, not one flesh by natural union, but one in a spiritual mode and by a spiritual efficacy, not in number?

units.la: Sed alia quoque & quidem grauissimi momenti in illis ipsorum verbis reprehendo. Quod enim aiunt fieri non posse, ut spirituales substantiæ, eo modo in essentia sua quo corporeæ substantiæ, sese visquam præsentes sistant, vere quidem dicitur, Angelis propter-ea, quoties sese oculis conspiciendos præbuerunt, humana corpora ad illum visum assu-mentibus, vel per imaginarias visiones appa-rentibus: & ipsa animarum nostrarum incor-porea substantia non aliter quàm interventu corporis à nobis intelligitur, nedum ut in i-psos oculos nostros incurrat. Sed quorsum hoc adversum nos? Nec enim Angelicam il-lam aut animabus nostris similem corporis & sanguinis Christi hic in terris vel in signis illis, vel apud corpora nostra præsentiam in his mysteriis imaginamur: sed illam tum ex nostræ fidei analogia, tum ex vero Sacramen-torum scopo,merè spiritualem esse docemus. Primùm enim, quòd ad Deum nobiscum de spirituali in Christo, & per Christum vita paciscentem attinet, quidquid hic promitti-tur , merè per Sp. Sancti prorsus divinam & cœlestem virtutem mentibus nostris præbe-
units.tr: But I also object to other things, and indeed of the greatest weight, in those very words of theirs. For when they say that spiritual substances cannot be present anywhere in their essence in the same way as corporeal substances, this is rightly said: angels, whenever they showed themselves to be seen by human eyes, took on human bodies for that sight, or appeared through imaginary visions; and the incorporeal substance of our own souls is understood by us only through the medium of the body, let alone that it falls under our own eyes. But what does this have to do with us? For we do not imagine that the presence of Christ's body and blood in these mysteries is like that angelic presence, or like that of our souls, here on earth, either in those signs or near our bodies. Rather, we teach that it is purely spiritual, both from the analogy of our faith and from the true purpose of the sacraments. For first, as far as God covenanting with us concerning spiritual life in Christ and through Christ is concerned, whatever is promised here is a purely spiritual mystery, given and bestowed upon our minds entirely by the divine and heavenly power of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Ende tur & præstatur,spirituale mysterium est. De-inde quòd ad credentes attinet, quibuscum ille Spiritualia illa omnia paciscitur: sicut Spirituali virtute mentibus nostris illa per si-gnorum demum analogiam, intelligenda & credenda vt in cœlis nobis reposita, non au-tem hic in terris oculis intuenda, & mani-bus vel ore sumenda præbentur & præ-stantur : ita vel à principiis suis disce-dant oportet, vel fateri necesse est,illa ἀναλο-γως non nisi spiritualiter, id est, per fidei in-strumentum percipi posse.Nam,obsecro,si in hominum meré humanis contractibus legi-timis res illæ ipsæ, de quibus inter pacifcen-tes conuenit,siue corporeæ sint siue incorpo-reæ, verè & reipsa vel inter paciscentes vt in societate (qualis est cœlestis iste inter Chri-stum & credentes contractus) communes siunt:vel vt in alienationum contractibus,il-lorum siunt in quos earum dominium & possessio transfertur : an non fuerit impietas eam vim ad apprehendendum verè ac reipsa, & communem sibi faciendum , immò sibi spiritualiter cocorporandū Christum ipsum-met cum suis omnibus beneficiis, vim & facultatem, illi pa[?]ctioni,divinæ prorsus ac cœ-lesti, & illi merè quoque supernaturali fidei instrumento divinitus ad hunc vsum incor-dibus nostris creato,detrahere?
units.tr: Next, as far as believers are concerned, with whom he makes covenant concerning all these spiritual things: just as those things are offered and bestowed upon our minds by spiritual power, to be understood and believed as laid up for us in heaven, and not to be looked at with the eyes here on earth, or taken with the hands or mouth, but only through the analogy of the signs, so they must either depart from their own principles or necessarily confess that these things can be grasped analogically only spiritually, that is, through the instrument of faith. For, I beg you, if in purely human lawful contracts those very things about which the parties agree, whether bodily or incorporeal, truly and actually become common to the contracting parties in a partnership (such as this heavenly contract between Christ and believers), or pass into the ownership and possession of those to whom they are transferred in contracts of alienation, would it not be impiety to deprive that agreement, divine and wholly heavenly, and that purely supernatural instrument of faith, divinely created in our hearts for this use, of the power and capacity to lay hold of Christ himself with all his benefits truly and actually, and to make him common to us, and to be spiritually made one body with him?

units.la: Deinde quòd corporales essentias illi di-cunt non aliter quàm corporali modo essen-tia sua præsentes posse statui, non est sine distinctione verum. Essentiae enim corporeae corporibus quidem sistere[?] se praesentes aliter quàm corporeo modo non possunt: sed quid sint, & quales sint(qua in re posita est vera illarum cognitio) à sensibus percipi & cognosci nequeunt, sed à solo intellectu, si quidem sanus est, verè & scienter: sin vero sanus non est,falsa duntaxat opinione,cognoscuntur.
units.tr: Next, their claim that corporeal essences can be present only in a corporeal mode is not true without distinction. For corporeal essences cannot indeed be present in bodies in any way other than in a bodily mode; but what they are and of what kind they are (on which true knowledge of them depends) cannot be perceived and known by the senses, but only by the intellect, truly and knowingly if it is sound; but if it is not sound, they are known only by false opinion.

units.la: Quocunque autem modo res siue corporeas, siue incorporeas consideret intellectus, nihil propterea in rebus ipsis mutatur. Itaque est cur merito de iis conqueramur, qui, propterea quòd sola vi merè spirituali, per fidei instrumentum, Christum ipsum, cum suis beneficiis nobis communicari, id est, noitram, atque adeò ex Evangelij pacto, Unum mysticum quiddam nobiscum, ad noitram inde hauriendam salutem, fieri affirmamus: concludunt corpus non verum, sed imaginarium, &c, quale est illorum Omnimaiestaticum & Ubiquitarium, Christo sic affingi. Item, & de iis qui, quoniam metonymico tropo Sacramentis omnibus usitatissimo, corporis ipsius pro nobis traditi nomen huic pani,& huic vino itidem sanguinis pro nobis fusi appellationem tribui dicimus, inde absurdissimè & ineptissimè colligunt verum illud corpus Christi,ut & sanguinem,in tropicum, ut invidiosè loquuntur, corpus & metonymicum nescio quem sanguinem à nobis transformari.
units.tr: However, in whatever way the intellect considers things, whether corporeal or incorporeal, nothing in the things themselves is changed by this. Therefore there is cause to complain justly of those who, because we affirm that Christ himself with his benefits is communicated to us by purely spiritual power through the instrument of faith, that is, that by the covenant of the Gospel he becomes one mystical thing with us, for drawing our salvation from him, conclude that a body that is not true but imaginary, and so on, such as their omnipresent and ubiquitous body, is thus attributed to Christ. Likewise, of those who, since we say that by metonymy, a trope most common in all sacraments, the name of the body given for us is given to this bread, and likewise the name of the blood shed for us to this wine, draw from this most absurdly and foolishly the conclusion that the true body of Christ, and his blood too, are transformed by us into a tropical body, as they spitefully put it, and into I know not what metonymic blood.

units.la: Et de his quidem omnibus hactenus,quae, si vera sunt, id est, omnibus Christianæ nostrę religionis capitibus, Apostolico symbolo, quod est totius divinæ Scripturæ epitome, divinitus dictato, comprehensis penitus consentanea: cur non omnes, quaeso, & singuli, quibus Deus ad agnoscendum magis ac magis Antichristum oculos aperuit, in hanc veritatem consentimus? Sin vero, ista vel penitus vel aliquatenus ab illa veritate discrepant, cur odiis, calumniis, virulentis denique omnibus conuitiis semel conceptas opiniones non sane constanter, sed quoquo modo retinentes, alij alios lacerare tamdiu malumus, quàm nos mutuò per illum placidissimum Christi spiritum, in sacro & legitimo conuentu [illegible, ~8 letters], & sic mutua Christiana ὁμοφρο-σύνῃ communes illos veritatis hostes, vel ad eiusdem veritatis consensionem pertrahere, vel magis ac magis arguere? Et qua de re potius vere Christianos omnes Reges, Principes, Magistratus denique cæteros, & quidé in primis Ecclesiarū Pastores laborare oportuit: Cur non, inquam, illud ipsum ultro inter nos agimus, quod toties à Pontificiis ipsis tato studio impetrare studuimus, nempe ut placidè nobiscum de controversiis religionis, ex puro Dei verbo, in libera & legitima Synodo conferre mallent, quàm innoxios, & ultrò fidei suæ confessionem edere, & tali collationi, cui Deus ipse præsideret sese subiicere paratos, omnis crudelitatis genere persequi? Hoc verò tantum & tam necessarium beneficium quod vix ab hominibus sperare licet, Æterne Deus & Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, a-gédum pro infinita bonitate tua & miseri-cordia largire. Hoc Iesu Christe Fili Dei, Patri ὁμοούσιε, [illegible, ~9 letters] ovicularum tibi a Patre donatarum custos & gubernator, nobis pro tua de iis, pro quibus tuam ipsius animā deposuisti, sollicitudine perpetua, tuorum te agnoscentium, & controversias istas serio detestā-tium precibus, lacrymis, gemitibus assiduis tribue. Hoc tu Sanctissime Spiritus, coæterne & coessentialis ille Patris & Filij, operum pręfertim sanctorum illorum, effector, Ecclesiæ, tam indignè domi & foris vexatæ doctor & consolator, concede omnibus, Abba Pater, te inspiratore, clamantibus: ut omnibus erro-rum tenebris, quoad eius fieri potest, quàm longissimè repulsis, in veritatem, quam nos doces, totis animis consentiamus: & non tan-tùm verbo, sed etiam reipsa hanc veritatem profitentes, per medias huius mundi tenebras ut filij lucis ambulemus: donec opere tuo plenissimè in nobis peracto, una cum Patre & Filio tecum unico vero Deo, in æternum beati, sempiternam in cœlis vitam vivamus. Amen.
units.tr: And so far enough of all these matters, which, if they are true, that is, wholly consonant with all the heads of our Christian religion, comprised in the Apostles' Creed, divinely dictated, which is the epitome of all divine Scripture, why, I ask, do we not all and each, to whom God has opened our eyes to recognise Antichrist more and more, agree to this truth? But if these things differ from that truth either wholly or in some degree, why do we prefer to tear one another apart for so long with hatreds, calumnies and, finally, every kind of virulent reproach, holding opinions once conceived not steadily but in whatever way, rather than, through that most peaceful spirit of Christ, in a sacred and lawful assembly [illegible], and so by mutual Christian harmony [homophrosyne], either draw those common enemies of the truth to agreement with the same truth or prove them more and more wrong? And for what reason should all Christian kings, princes and magistrates, and above all the ministers of the Churches, have laboured? Why, I say, do we not ourselves freely do that very thing which we have so often and with such zeal sought to obtain from the Papists: namely, that they would prefer to confer peacefully with us about the controversies of religion, from the pure Word of God, in a free and lawful Synod, rather than persecute with every kind of cruelty the innocent who voluntarily publish the confession of their faith, and be ready to submit to such a conference over which God himself would preside? But this great and necessary benefit, which can hardly be hoped for from men, Eternal God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, grant, we pray, according to your infinite goodness and mercy. Grant this, Jesus Christ, Son of God, consubstantial with the Father, [illegible], guardian and governor of the little sheep given to you by the Father, by your perpetual care for those for whom you laid down your own soul, to us who acknowledge you and earnestly detest these controversies, with prayers, tears and continual groans. Grant this, you Most Holy Spirit, co-eternal and co-essential with the Father and the Son, effector especially of those holy works, teacher and comforter of the Church so unworthily harassed at home and abroad, to all who cry, "Abba, Father," with you as their inspirer: that, with the darkness of errors driven back as far as possible, we may with all our souls assent to the truth which you teach, and, professing this truth not only in word but also in deed, may walk as children of light through the midst of the darkness of this world; until, your work being fully accomplished in us, together with the Father and the Son, you, the one true God, we may live eternal life in heaven, blessed for ever. Amen.
